A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same greedy interpretation of training-free guided generation. Their main text, equations, figures, and appendices support comparison, and retained results can be matched despite the changed title and extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 contains theoretical arguments, proofs, and conceptual diagrams. Section 6 explicitly states that no experimental work was included; the appendices contain no original empirical results.

after.justification: v2 reports original FFHQ inverse-image experiments and QM9 property-guided molecular generation in Section 7 and Appendices H–I, including quantitative results and generated examples.

M1.justification: The original posterior-gradient guidance remains. v2 adds concrete midpoint and two-step Euler gradient estimators and a scheduled molecular-guidance update (Section 6; Appendices H.2–H.3), refining the discretization tradeoff already suggested in v1.

E1.justification: v1 uses no experimental datasets. v2 adds eight inverse-image tasks on FFHQ, covering super-resolution, deblurring, inpainting, phase retrieval, and HDR reconstruction, plus QM9 generation targeting six molecular properties.

E2.justification: v1 discusses existing methods without empirical comparisons. v2 introduces task-specific comparisons against DAPS, DPS, DDRM, DDNM, DCDP, FPS-SMC, DiffPIR, and RED-diff in Tables 1 and 5. Table 2 additionally compares molecular guidance with DTO, described as essentially D-Flow, and unguided EquiFM.

E3.justification: v2 introduces complete evaluation protocols: 100 FFHQ images at 256 × 256 with measurement noise 0.05, PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS/FID evaluation, and specified sampling and optimization budgets. QM9 experiments introduce classifier-training and target-sampling procedures, L-BFGS guidance, property MAE, and atom/molecule stability metrics. These experiments have no counterparts in v1.

E4.justification: v2 adds solver-choice comparisons, molecular-stability analysis, and HDR sampling-trajectory case studies (Tables 1, 2, and 4; Figures 6–8). Appendix H.2 also reports RK4 instability and unsuccessful mixed-solver and endpoint-truncation remedies. v1 contains no comparable empirical analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix H newly states that fixed random seeds were used. Table 5 also includes ± terms for some nonlinear-task baseline results, although their meaning and repeated-run counts are unspecified. The new greedy-method results lack corresponding uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds all empirical scores, generated examples, and runtime measurements. Examples include greedy Euler's 30.87 dB PSNR for random inpainting in Table 1 and molecular polarizability MAEs of 11.282 for Euler, 5.313 for midpoint, and 1.404 for DTO in Table 2. These are newly reported results, not performance changes against v1 experiments.

T1.justification: The exact-flow, Euler-guidance, greedy-convergence, and control-adjoint results are retained and reorganized. v2 substantially extends the theory with covariance-based flow Jacobians, guidance-response differentials, gradient-error bounds, general Runge-Kutta gradient-accuracy results, and a flow reparameterization, with derivations in Appendices C–D.

C1.justification: The central unification claim and compute–accuracy tradeoff already appear in v1. v2 extends the stated contribution toward higher-order interpolation schemes and presents greedy usefulness more cautiously in its conclusion as reasonable for certain tasks. The overarching research claim remains intact.

C2.justification: v2 adds a covariance-projection explanation of guidance and interprets its new results as showing task-dependent benefits, molecular instability, and accuracy–stability tradeoffs. Appendices H.2 and J.2 discuss learning-rate failures, naive annealing, and unexplored mixed-accuracy schedules. The earlier adjoint caveats are retained and expanded into practical recommendations in Appendix E.

D1.justification: Appendix H adds model provenance, data-processing settings, noise schedules, optimizer configurations, guidance learning rates, and numerical-solver formulas. It also reports H100/V100 hardware, memory consumption, and runtime. v1 provides no corresponding experimental implementation information.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands research positioning around inverse problems, molecular generation, checkpointing, and numerical differentiation. Appendix A connects its two-step guidance to Moufad et al. (2025), adds further end-to-end approaches, and clarifies D-Flow's practical use of DTO with checkpointing. These changes extend the literature discussion beyond relocating v1's related work.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, and guidance exposition, and changes terminology to posterior guidance and end-to-end guidance. Related work, adjoint caveats, and control-signal analysis move into Appendices A, E, and F. Appendix navigation and a theoretical-results index accompany the reorganized narrative.

P2.justification: v2 reworks the existing conceptual diagrams, including a compact main-text taxonomy and an expanded appendix version. It adds five tables and extensive image, molecule, and trajectory displays, with substantial layout and caption changes. Figure 10 introduces a caption error: it shows box inpainting but labels it super-resolution.

improvement.justification: v1's practical case for greedy guidance rests entirely on theory and explicitly lacks experiments and gradient-response analysis. v2 adds substantial evidence and analysis, exposing molecular failures and limited benefits from extra computation alongside successful image applications. This makes its applicability and tradeoffs much better supported. Sparse uncertainty reporting and caption errors limit reporting quality, but the overall evidential gain is substantial.
